chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the glorification (Tasbih), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not know of any specific/regularized glorification other than the Tasbih of Fatima (peace be upon her); and ten times after the dawn prayer, you should say.'
'There is no god except Allah, Alone, there is no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom, and for Him is the Praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is Able over all things.'
And you may glorify (Allah) as much as you wish, voluntarily.

key_terms.تَسْبِيحِ فَاطِمَةَ: The Tasbih of Fatima (a specific devotional formula)
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَ يُمِيتُ: He gives life and causes death

ai.seo_question: What is the Tasbih of Fatima and when should it be recited according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Tasbih of Fatima (SA) as the preeminent regularized dhikr, emphasizing its unique status among morning and evening supplications. The text underscores the theological pillars of Tawhid, sovereignty, and divine omnipotence, while allowing for voluntary expansion of praise. This practice reflects the Shia tradition of linking daily spiritual discipline to the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the connection between prophetic guidance and familial intercession.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala Bin Razeyn, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Glorification (Tasbeeh). So heasws said: ‘Iasws do not know of anything other than the Tasbeeh of Fatimaasws; and ten times after Al-Fajr (Salat) you should be saying,

‘There is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Alone, there being no associates for Him<sup>azwj</sup>. For Him<sup>azwj</sup> is the Kingdom, and for Him<sup>azwj</sup> is the Praise; and He<sup>azwj</sup> Curses to live and He<sup>azwj</sup> Causes to die, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is Able upon everything’.
And then you can Glorify whatever you so desire to, voluntarily’.
en.sarwar: 34. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from ibn Mahbub from al- ‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Once I asked abu Ja’far (a.s.) about Tasbih (words to glorify Allah).

The Imam said, ‘I do not know of anything other than Tasbih of Fatimah (a.s.) and ten times after the morning prayer, ‘No one deserves to be worshipped except Allah, alone Who has no partner, to Him belongs all praise, He gives life, causes death.

He has power over all things,’ and then say Tasbih voluntarily as much as you wish.’” (! Tasbih of Fatimah (a.s.) consists of saying, ‘Allah is greater than can be described,’ thirty-four times ‘all praise belongs to Allah,’ thirty-three times and ‘Allah is free of defects,’ thirty-three times.)
